chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Isḥāq al-Baṭayḥī, who said:
I saw Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام perform the ʿishāʾ prayer before the disappearance of the twilight, then he departed.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: a kunyah referring to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام in this context
key_terms.ارْتَحَلَ: he departed or set out on a journey
key_terms.الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ: the night prayer, meaning the ʿishāʾ prayer
key_terms.سُقُوطِ الشَّفَقِ: the disappearance of twilight, a time marker related to prayer timing

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform the ʿishāʾ prayer before the twilight fully disappears?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام performed the ʿishāʾ prayer before the twilight had disappeared, and then set out. It is relevant to the jurisprudential discussion of the timing of maghrib and ʿishāʾ and indicates practical performance of the prayer within that time context.
